results.question: Describe one documented case where he reconciled conflicting metric definitions or reporting needs across country teams. What governance, quality checks and access safeguards did he personally establish, and what changed for the people using the reports?
results.answer:
As Data Director at Gozem, Bolaji established an enterprise metrics governance framework and a centralized metrics catalog to reconcile inconsistent metric definitions across analytics, reporting, and AI-powered workflows as the company expanded across multiple business domains and countries. To ensure data quality and governance, he standardized KPI computation through reusable BigQuery and Dataform assets, introduced automated data-quality checks, discrepancy alerts for incomplete data and duplicates, and performance tracking across 250+ production pipelines. For access safeguards, he built role-based access governance with 3 access tiers crossed with 3 team roles and introduced governed AI access via an MCP-enabled BigQuery integration in Claude, allowing selected senior users to query enterprise data within their existing Google Cloud IAM permissions. These efforts closed long-standing reporting disputes between Finance, Operations, and Product, providing a single source of truth for over 700 people collaborating across Benin, Togo, Gabon, Cameroon, and Congo.

Selected senior users could query enterprise data using natural language within their existing Google Cloud IAM permissions.

evidence.section: Enterprise metrics governance & AI-ready semantic layer
evidence.parent_context: Bolaji BALOGOUN · Biography > Data Director · GOZEM · Apr 2025 - Jul 2026
evidence.content_preview:
Source: 90_website_canon_llms_full.txt | Title: Bolaji BALOGOUN · Data Engineer · Data Architect (full content) | Section: Enterprise metrics governance & AI-ready semantic layer | Parent context: Bolaji BALOGOUN · Biography > Data Director · GOZEM · Apr 2025 - Jul 2026

Result: Established a single source of truth for business metrics across analytics, reporting, and AI-powered workflows.
Problem: As Gozem expanded its analytics footprint across multiple business domains and countries, the risk of inconsistent metric interpretation increased. KPI definitions, transformation logic, aggregation rules, dimensions, and query implementations were often embedded across dashboards, SQL queries, reports, and undocumented team knowledge.

At the same time, emerging AI-powered analytics workflows created new requirements. Business users needed trusted natural-language access to data, while AI agents required a reliable understanding of business concepts, metrics, and relationships to generate accurate insights.

The organization needed a foundation capable of serving both humans and AI systems with a consistent interpretation of business performance.
Solution: Designed and implemented the foundation of an enterprise metrics governance framework covering KPI definitions, source systems, transformation dependencies, aggregation behavior, available dimensions, lineage, and canonical calculation methods.

Created a centralized metrics catalog documenting how each KPI is derived, whether from raw operational data or transformed analytical models, including supporting business context, relationships between metrics, valid dimensions, joins, and calculation formulas.

Standardized KPI computation through reusable BigQuery and Dataform assets powering reporting and analytical applications, ensuring consistent metric definitions across dashboards, analyses, and operational workflows.

Introduced governed AI access to warehouse data through an MCP-enabled BigQuery integration in Claude. Selected senior users could query enterprise data using natural language within their existing Google Cloud IAM permissions.

This work also laid the foundations for an AI-ready semantic layer capable of supporting future copilots, autonomous agents, self-service analytics experiences, and automated decision-support systems.
Tools: BigQuery · Dataform · MCP · Claude · Python · Looker Studio · Google Cloud IAM
